transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Alex Gomez (Head of ML, IronPeak), Priya Nair (Platform Lead), Ben Carter (Security)

Summary: quick discovery to understand IronPeak's capacity & security requirements for dedicated GPUs; gather traffic patterns and success criteria; discuss burst strategy, isolation, scaling, and pricing.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, uh thanks for joining, i'm jordan from redwood, this is maya our se. how are you all?
[00:12] Alex Gomez: good thanks, alex here. excited to dig in, we, we have a lot of questions about dedicated capacity and how it fits our infra.
[00:24] Priya Nair: hi, priya, platform lead. timing on this is pretty tight — legal/procurement wants an initial proposal by next week.
[00:34] Ben Carter: ben from security — i'll be focusing on data isolation, encryption, and audit logs.
[00:44] Maya Chen: great, quick agenda — current stack, workloads (qps and seq len), isolation needs, burst patterns, security reqs, and next steps. sound ok?
[00:56] Alex Gomez: yep, go for it.
[01:08] Jordan Lee: first q — what's your current infra for inference? are you running self-hosted endpoints on kubernetes, or using a managed API?
[01:20] Alex Gomez: currently we run in-house on k8s with nvidia a100s, mix of on-prem and cloud GPUs. it's getting expensive and ops heavy, especially for model updates. we looked at hosted apis but data retention and pii concerns are the blocker.
[01:44] Maya Chen: got it — so dedicated would give you reserved pools and isolation. do you plan to move all inference to dedicated or hybrid (hosted + dedicated)?
[01:56] Priya Nair: hybrid likely — low-latency/PII-sensitive routes on dedicated, less-sensitive batch jobs could go to hosted. we want deterministic SLAs for key flows.
[02:10] Jordan Lee: good, what's your baseline and peak qps, and typical sequence lengths?
[02:18] Alex Gomez: baseline is about 20 qps for our core model (LLM-8k-ish, actually we're using a tuned Llama variant). peak end-of-day burst can hit 180-220 qps for 20-30 minutes. seq len average 256 tokens, but some sessions go up to 1k for longer context.
[02:40] Maya Chen: ok that helps — for sizing dedicated pools we look at model, quantization, latency targets — what's your p99 latency goal?
[02:50] Priya Nair: 300ms p99 for the core route, ideally under 200ms if we can.
[02:58] Ben Carter: and we need data to never leave our vpc, or at minimum be encrypted and logged; we need KMS with customer-managed keys.
[03:12] Jordan Lee: yep, Redwood Dedicated supports VPC peering and private deployments, and you can bring your own KMS/HSM — we also provide audit logs and extended retention as an add-on. i'll share SOC2 and network diagrams after the call.
[03:30] Alex Gomez: quick Q — does dedicated allow bursting beyond reserved capacity? our traffic is spiky and we don't want customer-visible throttling.
[03:40] Maya Chen: yes — options: reserved baseline with burst credits to shared capacity (subject to availability), or guaranteed burst via committed burst capacity add-on. tradeoff is cost predictability vs absolute availability. we can propose a mix.
[03:58] Priya Nair: curious about autoscaling speed — how quickly can you add nodes to handle burst? and is KV cache preserved across scale events?
[04:12] Maya Chen: autoscaling is configurable; for Dedicated we can do pre-warmed instances and fast scaling (tens of seconds to a couple minutes) — but the real speed depends on model warmup and kv cache rebuild. we use prefix/KV caching to keep latency low; cache warm-up can be mitigated by pre-warming or traffic mirroring during a canary.
[04:36] Alex Gomez: so for that 200 qps burst, we'd want pre-warmed nodes to avoid cold start lag. what's the cost delta for pre-warmed vs on-demand?
[04:48] Jordan Lee: pre-warmed instances are charged as reserved capacity (so higher commitment) but give predictable latency. on-demand bursts use dynamic capacity at usage rates — cheaper but less predictable. i'll include example pricing scenarios in the proposal.
[05:02] Ben Carter: on encryption — do you support customer-managed keys in their HSM, and can logs be sent to our SIEM? we need tamper-evident logs.
[05:14] Maya Chen: yes, we integrate with major KMS providers and can forward logs to your syslog/SIEM. audit logs include per-request metadata and model versions; tamper-evidence is via append-only storage and signed log bundles for compliance reviews.
[05:38] Priya Nair: what's your model catalog policy? we need to run our tuned Llama variant; can you host custom models in Dedicated?
[05:48] Jordan Lee: Dedicated supports customer-provided models — we assist with model packaging and optimizing kernels. there are also Redwood-curated models if you prefer.
[06:02] Alex Gomez: performance — any public benchmarks for 256-token seq on a dedicated pool vs hosted?
[06:10] Maya Chen: we have internal perf profiles for common GPUs and models — i'll pull a few reference numbers for tuned Llama-like models. note that quantization and kernel selection affect throughput heavily.
[06:26] Alex Gomez: ok, also licensing — what's the typical contract length and how do commits map to capacity?
[06:34] Jordan Lee: typical is monthly or annual reserved capacity with options to scale; commits give you guaranteed throughput and lower unit costs. we'll include both monthly and annual options in the quote.
[06:48] Priya Nair: timeline: we want a pilot in two weeks, with a small dedicated pool to validate latency and integration. legal wants pricing and security docs for internal approval this week.
[07:00] Jordan Lee: understood — we can target a pilot starting 3/10. i'll send the docs today.
[07:10] Ben Carter: a couple of security edge cases — data residency for EU customers; do you support region pinning for Dedicated deployments?
[07:20] Maya Chen: yes, region pinning and physical isolation are supported in our Private and Dedicated offerings; we can ensure capacity in specific cloud regions and VPC peering to your subnets.
[07:34] Alex Gomez: curious about rolling updates — we need canary deployments and automatic fallbacks to a previous model if quality drops.
[07:42] Maya Chen: rollouts are supported — canary, A/B, and automated fallback policies tied to latency or quality signals. we also integrate with eval tooling to detect regressions.
[07:56] Jordan Lee: let's walk through a rough sizing scenario — baseline 20qps, p99 300ms, model with roughly 0.5 tokens per ms? (mumbling) may be off, maya correct me.
[08:12] Maya Chen: rough calc: 20 qps * 0.3s = 6 concurrent requests; for 200 qps burst that's 60 concurrent. translate to gpus depends on model/quantization — might be 1-2 GPUs baseline, 6-8 GPUs pre-warmed for burst — we'll produce a more precise estimate.
[08:36] Alex Gomez: that helps. also want to understand failure modes — if a node goes down during burst, do requests failover to hosted fallback?
[08:46] Maya Chen: yes, smart routing can fallback to hosted variants or other regions; you can configure graceful degradation policies.
[08:58] Priya Nair: about observability — we need token-level cost, per-route latency, and tracing across requests.
[09:08] Jordan Lee: Redwood Console provides per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, tracing, and error analysis. we can grant access to your SREs for the pilot.
[09:20] Ben Carter: one more: can you redact PII before sending logs to Redwood, or does dedicated keep raw logs in our environment?
[09:30] Maya Chen: in Dedicated, logs can be routed to your SIEM or retained by Redwood with configurable retention and redaction. for Private deployments full control stays with you.
[09:46] Alex Gomez: sounds promising. question about support SLAs for Dedicated — uptime and latency guarantees?
[09:54] Jordan Lee: we offer SLA-backed uptime for Dedicated plus priority support options; latency SLOs are tied to provisioning and are part of the contract.
[10:06] Priya Nair: perfect. for the proposal, please include a couple of capacity scenarios (baseline + burst), pricing models, and the SOC2/network docs.
[10:18] Jordan Lee: will do. any final Qs?
[10:22] Ben Carter: i'll follow up with a list of required compliance artifacts.
[10:28] Alex Gomez: ok, we're good. thanks.
[10:32] Jordan Lee: thanks everyone — recap: we send pricing and SOC2/docs, maya will do throughput estimates, priya to share traffic patterns, ben to confirm KMS needs; target pilot week of 3/10. i'll follow up with calendar invite for the kickoff.
[10:48] Priya Nair: thanks, talk soon.
